tools.description: Sign in with the server's configured account. miniserve gates every file operation (list, read, upload, mkdir, rm) behind HTTP basic auth, so you must sign in before doing anything with files; the session it opens is what authorizes you. Note: miniserve has no self-registration — accounts are fixed in the server config.

tools.description: End the current session so subsequent file operations are refused until you sign in again.

tools.description: Upload a file into the served tree so it can be listed and read back. Creates a File row at the given full path, carrying its content. Fails if an entry already exists at that path (delete it first), or if you are not signed in.

size.description: Optional byte size of the file; recorded so directory-size reads can total it.

summary: miniserve is a self-hosted static-file HTTP server (Rust, actix-web); the persisted state is the filesystem served under a root dir. It uploads/moves file and directory entries (POST /upload, POST /rm for delete) and reads them back via directory listing, raw file download, and archive/dir-size readops; optional HTTP basic auth checks a config-defined AuthAccount list.
_drops: file_download_archive (GET <dir>?download=tar|tar.gz|zip): in reality a binary byte-stream archive of a whole subtree — it has no row-level semantics as a File search, so it was dropped rather than exposed as a meaningless global table read.
file_upload's file_hash / file_hash_function params: inert X-File-Hash integrity headers bound to no column; dropped to keep the upload panel to path/name/content.
file_list's sort / order / download / raw params: HTTP-UI listing modifiers that do not map to runtime table behavior; the panel keeps path + name search.
